The related question is the same as the paired revision's: was she First Lady of the United States (a stored title, counted 118 times as 'Eleanor Roosevelt, First Lady of the United States', that follows from the marriage and FDR's presidency in 2 hops); who FDR was married to (the symmetric reading of the removed fact) was dropped as the same knowledge restated. No stored husband-phrased sentence reaches 100 counts, so the husband's own office is not used. Caveat: the title is about her, not a third individual. Caveats: Churchill's marriage to Clementine is stored and, with spouse_of functional and symmetric, still gives 'no', so a clean removal can keep 'no' for Churchill; 'the longest-serving First Lady' encodes the marriage (a First Lady is the president's wife), so the binding answer can come back without the removed fact.
